title: Shopify Review (2026)
intro: Shopify is evaluated here as a hosted SaaS ecommerce platform — Shopify is a hosted ecommerce platform for building an online store, managing catalog and orders, selling across channels, and scaling to retail POS and enterprise Plus. US list pricing (2026-08-26): Basic $39/mo or $29/mo billed yearly; Grow $105/$79; Advanced $399/$299; Plus from $2,300/mo. Current promo (shopify.com/pricing, 26 Aug 2026): 3-day free trial, then $1/mo for 3 months on eligible plans; Plus trial at $399. Shopify Payments lowers online card rates by plan (e.g. 2.9% + 30¢ Basic, 2.5% + 30¢ Advanced). This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s Ecommerce methodology, scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Shopify when you want the default hosted ecommerce platform — fast launch, strong checkout, channels, and a proven scale path.
verdict: Choose Shopify when you want the default hosted ecommerce platform — fast launch, strong checkout, channels, and a proven scale path. Consider BigCommerce for multi-storefront GMV packaging; WooCommerce for WordPress/open-source control; Square Online if in-person POS is the center of gravity. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Shopify’s guided admin, theme editor, and app ecosystem let most merchants launch without developers — scored from first-party positioning, not hands-on lab testing.
Primary job is hosted ecommerce — storefront, catalog, checkout, and channels are core product surfaces, not bolt-ons.
Variants, inventory locations, orders, and fulfillment workflows scale to mid-market and Plus — held below bespoke ERP depth.
Shopify Checkout and Shop Pay are conversion strengths; plan-level processing rates improve on higher tiers.
Large app store plus native channel connectors (social, marketplaces) — ecosystem is a platform differentiator.
POS Lite on Basic and full POS on higher tiers support retail extensions — strong but not every merchant needs POS.
Plus, multi-location inventory, and automation (Flow) support high GMV brands — enterprise path is clear.
Headline plans are competitive but apps, themes, and processing spreads compress value on growing stores.
Shopify Magic / Sidekick ship native AI for merchandising and ops — useful, not the primary purchase driver.

bestFor: Merchants wanting a hosted store without managing infrastructure
Brands scaling across online + retail channels
Teams that value app ecosystem over building custom stacks
notIdealFor: Merchants who need full code ownership on day one with zero subscription
Pure dropshipping-only workflows with no storefront ambition
Buyers optimizing solely for lowest processing spread at tiny volume
pros: Best-in-class hosted storefront + checkout bundle for most DTC brands
Strong POS and payments story for omnichannel
cons: TCO rises with apps, themes, and non-Shopify Payments
Advanced customization can require dev help
limitations: Subscription plus apps/themes and payment spreads raise TCO versus headline plan price
Third-party payment gateways incur additional transaction fees on lower tiers
Plus and advanced B2B features require higher plans or add-ons
Heavy customization may need Liquid/dev resources or agency help
pricingSummary: From $39/mo Basic ($29 annual). Grow $105 ($79 annual). Advanced $399 ($299 annual). Plus from $2,300/mo. Promo (26 Aug 2026): 3-day free trial, then $1/mo × 3 months on eligible plans; Plus try $399. Confirm live promos on shopify.com/pricing.
whoShouldChoose: Choose Shopify when you want the default hosted ecommerce platform — fast launch, strong checkout, channels, and a proven scale path.
whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Consider BigCommerce for multi-storefront GMV packaging; WooCommerce for WordPress/open-source control; Square Online if in-person POS is the center of gravity.
